lines.say: A polygon with n sides has n corners and n interior angles.
Pentagon 5, hexagon 6, octagon 8, decagon 10.
A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal.
Here's a pentagon. How do we find the total of its angles?
Draw every diagonal from one corner. The pentagon splits into 3 triangles.

draw.alt: Diagonals from A split the pentagon into three triangles

lines.say: Each triangle is 180 degrees. 3 times 180 is 540.
There are always two fewer triangles than sides.
So the angle sum is n minus 2, times 180.
A pentagon has angles 100, 115, 120, 95 and x.
lines.alt: Pentagon with one unknown angle x

lines.say: The angle sum is 540. The known angles add to 430.
So x is 110 degrees.
All angles of a regular polygon are equal. So divide the sum by n.
Regular octagon. 6 times 180 is 1080. Divide by 8 to get 135.
lines.alt: Regular octagon with one interior angle marked

lines.say: Only regular polygons have equal angles. Don't divide an irregular one.
Extend one side. The angle outside is the exterior angle.
lines.alt: Regular hexagon with interior 120 degrees and exterior 60 degrees

lines.say: Walk around the park. At each corner you turn by the exterior angle.

draw.alt: Turning arrows at each corner of a pentagon

lines.say: Back at the start you've turned one full turn. So they add to 360.
For a regular octagon, each exterior angle is 360 over 8, which is 45.
Then the interior angle is 180 minus 45, which is 135. Same answer.
Each interior angle is 156. How many sides?
lines.alt: Interior angle 156 degrees with exterior angle marked

lines.say: First find the exterior angle. 180 minus 156 is 24.
Then 360 divided by 24 is 15. It has 15 sides.
If 360 doesn't divide exactly, that regular polygon can't exist.
Not n times 180. It's n minus 2, times 180.
Don't divide 360 by the interior angle. Use the exterior angle.
Two fewer triangles than sides.
Walk the park, turn 360.
Inside plus outside is 180.
Quick route to n: 360 divided by the exterior angle.
